cards.explanation: The answer is that He will not be consulted by them. The elders sat down expecting a word, and God says, "As surely as I live, I will not be consulted by you…" (Ezekiel 20:3). He backs it with an oath on His own life. Those elders walked in with a question and got a closed door, friends, and I'd be checking my pockets for my keys.

The answer is that God swore to bring them out into a land He picked for them. He swore to bring them out of Egypt into a land He had searched out for them. He calls it a land flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands (Ezekiel 20:6). He didn't just pick a spot, friends. He went looking.

The answer is the idols of Egypt. God tells them, "…you must not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt. I am the LORD your God." (Ezekiel 20:7). Throw away the abominations before your eyes, and stay clear of Egypt's idols. He says who He is right alongside the command.

The answer is True. God says, "None of them cast away the abominations before their eyes, and they did not forsake the idols of Egypt." (Ezekiel 20:8). Not a few of them, friends. NONE of them. That's about as complete as it gets.

The answer is the nations they were living among. God acted so His name would not be profaned in the eyes of the nations among whom they were living (Ezekiel 20:9). Those nations had seen Him reveal Himself to Israel by bringing them out of Egypt. His name was on the line in front of them.

The answer is so they'd know He's the LORD who makes them holy. God says the Sabbaths are "…a sign between us, so that they would know that I am the LORD who sanctifies them." (Ezekiel 20:12). Sanctifies means He's the one who makes them holy. The Sabbath was a reminder of who was doing the work.

The answer is False. God says they did not follow His statutes, they rejected His ordinances, and they utterly profaned His Sabbaths (Ezekiel 20:13). He even repeats that the man who does these things will live by them. They had the gift in their hands and walked away from it.

The answer is land. God swore He would not bring that generation into "…the land that I had given them—a land flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands—" (Ezekiel 20:15). It's the same land He had picked out for them. That oath is a heavy one, friends.

The answer is hearts. God says it was because "…their hearts continually went after their idols." (Ezekiel 20:16). That's where their hearts kept going, and notice the word continually. It's the reason God gives for the oath.

The answer is False. God says, "Yet I looked on them with pity and did not destroy them or bring them to an end in the wilderness." (Ezekiel 20:17). They had earned a hard oath about the land, but He did not end them. Pity is the word the verse uses.

The answer is the LORD's statutes. God says to the children, "I am the LORD your God; walk in My statutes, keep My ordinances, and practice them." (Ezekiel 20:19). First He says what not to follow, then He says what to follow. His own word is the path, friends.

The answer is False. God says the children did not walk in His statutes or carefully observe His ordinances, and they profaned His Sabbaths (Ezekiel 20:21). He had told them what to do and what to avoid. They rebelled anyway.

The answer is that He'll scatter them among the nations. God swears He would "…scatter them among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands." (Ezekiel 20:23). The reason He gives is that they rejected His statutes, profaned His Sabbaths and fixed their eyes on their fathers' idols (Ezekiel 20:24). It's a serious oath, friends.

The answer is on any high hill or under any leafy tree. The text says, "…they saw any high hill or leafy tree, there they offered their sacrifices…" (Ezekiel 20:28). They also presented offerings, sent up incense and poured out drink offerings. Those are the places the verse names.

The answer is provoked. God says they "…presented offerings that provoked Me…" (Ezekiel 20:28). They were sending up incense and pouring out drink offerings, and it provoked Him. Offerings can be given the wrong way, friends.

The answer is Bamah. God asks, "What is this high place to which you go?" and the verse adds, "(And to this day it is called Bamah.)" (Ezekiel 20:29). The name stuck, and it was still the name when this was written.

The answer is True. God says, "…you continue to defile yourselves with all your idols to this day." (Ezekiel 20:31). It wasn't only their fathers, friends. Right up to the day Ezekiel spoke, the same habit was going on.

The answer is wood and stone. They say, "Let us be like the nations, like the peoples of the lands, serving wood and stone…" (Ezekiel 20:32). Wood and stone are the idols they wanted to serve. God answers what they have in mind.
The answer is False. God says, "what you have in mind will never come to pass." (Ezekiel 20:32). Never is a strong word, friends. Their plan to be like the nations is not going to happen.

The answer is gather. God says, "With a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and outpoured wrath I will bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the lands to which you have been scattered." (Ezekiel 20:34). The same hand that scatters is the hand that gathers.

The answer is that He will enter into judgment face to face. He says, "…I will bring you into the wilderness of the nations, where I will enter into judgment with you face to face." (Ezekiel 20:35). Face to face is the phrase God uses. It's a judgment meeting in the wilderness of the nations.

The answer is False. God says He will bring the rebels out of the land where they live, "…but they will not enter the land of Israel." (Ezekiel 20:38). Then the people will know He is the LORD. Those who rebel are purged out.

The answer is that they will surely listen to Him. God says, "Go and serve your idols, every one of you. But afterward, you will surely listen to Me…" (Ezekiel 20:39). Surely is a strong word, friends. The story doesn't end with the idols.

The answer is on His holy mountain. God says, "For on My holy mountain, the high mountain of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, there the whole house of Israel, all of them, will serve Me in the land." (Ezekiel 20:40). He says it about the whole house of Israel, all of them. His holy mountain is the place.

The answer is True, and what a turn. He says, "There I will accept them and will require your offerings and choice gifts, along with all your holy sacrifices." (Ezekiel 20:40). The One who said He would not be consulted now says He will accept them. Same God, new chapter for His people, friends.

The answer is aroma. God says, "…I will accept you as a pleasing aroma." (Ezekiel 20:41). That promise comes when He brings them from the peoples and gathers them from the lands where they were scattered. Pleasing is the word He uses.

The answer is that they will loathe themselves. The text says, "There you will remember your ways and all the deeds with which you have defiled yourselves, and you will loathe yourselves for all the evils you have done." (Ezekiel 20:43). It's a heavy line, friends. The remembering and the loathing are both right there in the same verse.

The answer is wicked. God says, "…when I have dealt with you for the sake of My name and not according to your wicked ways and corrupt acts, declares the Lord GOD." (Ezekiel 20:44). He deals with them for the sake of His name. He doesn't deal with them according to their ways.
